is_anopheles.evidence: The study analyzes insecticide susceptibility in Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus (page 3, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper is a meta-analysis of bioassay data. While L1014F and L1014S are mentioned in the discussion citing previous literature (page 23), no primary marker genotyping was performed.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies are presented; the extracted data only include bioassay knockdown times and mortality.

african_field_population.evidence: The included literature synthesized in the review covers field-collected populations across various African countries (page 3, Abstract).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is explicitly a meta-analysis and systematic review: 'Susceptibility Status of Principal Malaria Vectors to Insecticides Commonly Used for Malaria Control in Africa: Meta-analysis and Systemic review' (page 1, Title; page 3, Abstract).

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper compiles data from published studies and aggregates them by African region and insecticide.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study aggregates literature published from 2002 to 2021.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable; this is a systematic review of existing published literature.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary files contain additional bioassay data from included literature, not primary genotyping data.

assessment.summary: This article is a systematic review and meta-analysis summarizing bioassay susceptibility (knockdown time and mortality) data of Anopheles gambiae s.l. and An. funestus across Africa from 2002 to 2021. It does not report primary empirical research or extractable insecticide resistance marker genotype data.
